title: Partner marketplace quick-win asset sprint notes
body:
Goal: produce the minimal, high-quality asset set that lets a partner (or internal PM) ship a marketplace tile within a 2-week sprint. Focus on copy clarity, technical acceptance gates, and the smallest set of localized assets that unblock publishing and early conversion experiments.

Context / constraints:
- This is a quick-win backlog item to accelerate partner listings for cloud marketplaces (AWS/GCP/Azure). Not the full enterprise package.
- Must be deployable by partner engineering with our minimal onboarding steps; legal/compliance signoff handled in parallel but called out where needed.
- Keep designs small: 1 hero screenshot, 1 16:9 usage image, small square icon (128/256 px), 1 short video optional.

Prioritized deliverables (MVP):
1) Title + 60-char strapline + 220-char blurb (finalized copy variants)
2) 400–900 char long description with 3 bullets (problem, solution, differentiation)
3) Quickstart snippet: 3 lines of code or curl that show a value prop (generate text / embeddings example)
4) Technical acceptance checklist (below) signed by partner eng owner
5) Visuals: icon, hero screenshot, one in-product screenshot, alt text for each image
6) Billing SKU mapping + trial entitlement notes (how trial is provisioned)
7) Support & SLA blurb + link to docs; contact for escalations
8) 2 CTA options: "Get started" (free trial) and "Contact sales" (for enterprise)

Copy variants (work-in-progress):
- Strapline (<=60 chars): "High‑throughput LLM inference, production scale"
- 220-char blurb: "Run fast, reliable large‑language models with predictable latency and lower per‑token cost. Redwood Inference provides hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with built‑in observability and autoscaling—ready for production workloads."
- 400-char long description (sketch): "Redwood Inference delivers a single API for serving high‑performance LLM models across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Ship production features with predictable latency, cost controls (batching, caching, quantization), and rollout tooling. Ideal for teams that need SLAs, data controls, and clear unit economics. Includes SDKs, examples, and a simple billing mapping for marketplace trials."
- 3 bullets for marketplace UI:
  • Predictable latency and autoscaling for production traffic
  • Cost controls: batching, cache, quantization profiles
  • Private deployment options and audit logs for compliance

Quickstart snippet (curl example - small, copy-targeted):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood‑open‑fast-1","input":"Summarize our Q4 roadmap in 2 bullets","max_tokens":60}'

Technical acceptance checklist (must be confirmed by partner eng):
- Endpoint reachability from partner's marketplace deployment flow (test URL + sample request)
- Example API key flow for provisioning trial credentials (documented & automated if possible)
- Metering proof: reported tokens or compute units match partner metering contract (sample CSV or API report)
- Billing mapping: SKU id and trial period clearly stated; cancellation flow noted
- Security notes: TLS enforced, TLS cert details documented, public IPs or allowed CIDRs listed if required by partner
- Data residency: where logs/metrics/backups may live; opt‑out options documented
- SSO/SCIM readiness: if partner requires SSO, show SAML/SCIM support and a contact for integration
- Support escalation path: email + phone (if required by partner), plus SLAs for trial vs paid customers
- Minimum test matrix executed: 1x short sequence (<=128 tokens), 1x mid (512), 1x long (2048) with latency and error recordings

Localization & image alt text notes:
- Primary locale: en-US. Localize short strapline and bullets for en-GB and de-DE in follow-up sprint.
- Alt text must be descriptive and <=125 characters; include product name early.

Acceptance criteria for product team (internal):
- Marketplace tile passes partner's technical QA and shows in staging catalog
- Copy approved by GTM lead and legal has no blocking comments
- Trial provisioning works end-to-end (user signs up, receives trial SKU, can make at least one successful API call)
- Telemetry captured: conversion from tile clicks -> signup -> successful API call tracked in analytics

Risks & mitigation (quick notes):
- Risk: partner requires custom integration for billing metering. Mitigation: scope an adapter (1–2 engineer days) and ship with a labeled limitation on the tile initial release.
- Risk: imagery shows PII or customer data; Mitigation: scrub screenshots and use synthetic/demo data.
- Risk: QA/Legal slow down. Mitigation: flag early, provide our standard marketplace legal template to partner counsel.

Owners & short timeline (2-week sprint plan):
- Sprint kickoff (Day 0): Aisha (lead) + Partner PM + Diego (design lead) + Evan (partner eng)
- Day 1–3: finalize short/220/long copy variants; design: hero + 1 screenshot
- Day 4–7: eng: quickstart snippet + trial provisioning + metering sample
- Day 8–10: partner tech QA + localization stub for en-GB and de-DE
- Day 11–12: collect legal signoff and finalize support blurb
- Day 13–14: staging publish + tracking smoke tests

Open questions (for partner kick-off):
- Can partner support our preferred trial provisioning flow (API token issuance) or do they require marketplace-managed entitlements?
- Any mandatory legal copy variants or mandatory icons (brand constraints)?
- Is single-tenant private deployment required for initial trial customers in their marketplace?

Immediate todo (today):
- Draft the 60-char strapline + 220-blurb and share in #mp-listings channel for quick feedback (Owner: Aisha, Due: EOD)
- Diego: mockup hero screenshot and produce 3 x size variants (Due: Day 3)
- Evan: validate token issuance flow against partner sandbox and attach sample curl to this doc (Due: Day 5)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep copy punchy, avoid jargon on the short blurb; save nuance for long description and docs links.
- If we can't get a video, a quick animated GIF showing low-latency response is often acceptable.
- Track one metric: "tile -> working API call" conversion; use that to prioritize follow-ups (ex: improve quickstart snippet).

References / links to templates:
- Our tile image guidelines: confluence:image-guidelines-v2
- Trial flow reference implementation: github:platform/trial-provisioning-sample
- Past listing we can reuse tone from: confluence:MP-legacy-tile-0901
